_comment: The current targeting snapshot, loaded by `manage.py targeting_import --from-manifest`. Rebuilding this dataset from source costs 30-45 minutes of API calls and can exhaust WorldPop's daily quota for everyone else, so a new environment should restore from here rather than re-fetch. Pin a new drive_file_id whenever the dataset changes materially: export, upload to the folder below (shared with connect-labs-sa), and update the id, created_at and counts in one commit so the file and the record stay together.
notes: Restore with: make manage CMD="targeting_import --from-manifest" (needs LABS_SYNTHETIC_GDRIVE_SA_KEY; already in the ECS task definition, and locally readable from Secrets Manager as labs-jj-synthetic-gdrive-sa-key with the labs AWS profile). Values went 54,136 -> 90,882 because three raster sources joined the API ones. The Malaria Atlas Project's 5 km surfaces give malaria as COUNTS at every level -- 241.9M P. falciparum cases and 645,961 deaths for Africa, against the WHO World Malaria Report's ~246M and ~569k -- which is what lets a treatment programme be sized rather than merely located. WorldPop's 1 km UN-adjusted grid finished the population backfill that its own statistics API had refused: ADM1 754 -> 778, ADM2 1,005 -> 1,517 of 1,518. And the two together answer physical access: 242.9M people in Africa live more than two hours' walk from a health facility. cc-by-3.0 is new in the licence list and is MAP's; it permits commercial use with attribution. Research notes are NOT in this snapshot -- they live in git and are written by `manage.py seed_targeting_research`, which should be run after any import.
